A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POROver research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix C report original Phi-3 finetuning, preference-optimization and human-annotation results.

after.justification: The main results and Appendix D report original experiments across multiple students, teachers and adversarial attacks, alongside retained Phi-3 results.

M1.justification: The overgeneration, rejection sampling, preference-pair construction, containment-threshold rule and DPO procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 formalize previously described steps; additional teacher and student configurations reuse the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Section 3.3.4 adds JailBreakBench with 100 prompts evaluated under GCG, PAIR and hand-crafted JBC attacks, substantially extending coverage to adversarial input conditions. The original training datasets and capability, safety and overrefusal benchmarks remain represented.

E2.justification: The GPT-3/GPT-3.5 baselines and random, DeBERTa, ArmoRM and Llama Guard 2 selection comparisons remain. New experiments reuse these comparator sets. Llama-3-70B is an alternative teacher configuration, while GCG, PAIR and JBC are attack conditions; no new competing alignment method is evaluated.

E3.justification: The experimental design expands from Phi-3-7B to five students, adding Llama-3.1-8B, Falcon-3-7B and Llama-3.2-3B/11B, plus a Llama-3-70B teacher configuration. New protocols include transferred Vicuna attack artifacts, attack-success-rate evaluation and an ASD grid adding 5,000 and 10,000 examples. The retained Phi-3 decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds adversarial robustness tests, student/teacher generalization checks, finer safety-data saturation analysis in Section 4.3 and qualitative threshold-sensitivity findings in Section 4.2. Figures 7–8 add teacher-response case comparisons. The original human-versus-automatic annotation analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means with standard errors and error bars. Neither specifies repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. The expanded results do not establish a changed statistical estimation practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for new students, the open-weight teacher and jailbreak attacks. Its headline OR-Bench F1 comparison changes from Phi-3's 70.81 to 88.33 to Llama-3.1-8B's 74.39 to 91.78, using different student and selection settings. Retained Phi-3 safety results match Table 7 and Figures 10–11, but its AlpacaEval results and additional-benchmark results from v1 Figure 4 are omitted.

T1.justification: The Llama Guard 2 score-normalization equation and preference-selection mathematics are unchanged. The new pseudocode restates existing procedures; neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly frames POROver as targeting already highly safe but overrefusing models and claims that no existing post-training method specifically targets this setting. The three central contributions concerning general-purpose overgeneration, toxic-prompt overgeneration and preference optimization remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of unconditional compliance at zero toxic preference data, low usefulness at the opposite threshold extreme and diminishing returns from additional safety data. Limitations shift from a single student family/size to unresolved scaling near teacher size and language/domain transfer. It also newly interprets POROver as preserving adversarial robustness, although Table 6 shows increased GCG and PAIR attack success.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies ten epochs, 40 warm-up steps, checkpoint-selection rules, evaluation frequency and GPU hours; additional model-specific decoding and generation settings are documented. These disclosures do not establish changes to earlier runs. Conversely, v2 omits v1's selected threshold of 0.01, its 2,013-plus-166 preference-sample breakdown and several exact checkpoint links. The code/data access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 positions POROver explicitly as complementary to traditional safety alignment. v2 adds references supporting the new models, jailbreak evaluations and reward-model choices, including RewardBench and OpenAssistant, while removing several reinforcement-learning references such as Dai, Kundu and Pang. The overall research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, results and limitations undergo substantial rewriting. Llama-3.1-8B becomes the main experimental narrative, retained Phi-3 results move to Appendix D, limitations move to Appendix A, and the supplementary narrative is reorganized by evaluation and model.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format. It adds algorithm blocks, response-comparison figures, a saturation plot and numerous model-specific and adversarial displays. Retained Phi-3 figures are relocated, its results table loses the AlpacaEval column, and the main capability table is restructured.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's explicit single-family/single-size evidence gap through multiple student families and sizes, an open-weight teacher and adversarial evaluation. Added sensitivity analyses and training details strengthen validation and reproducibility. Qualifications include omitted Phi-3 results and preference-data details, plus overstated robustness preservation: Table 6's GCG and PAIR attack success rises from 0.08 to 0.13 and 0.16 to 0.22 after POROver. These weaknesses temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial improvement in empirical support.
